Other: This is the reference assessment of when the ubiquitous minimal active space is good enough. Spin-orbit coupling constants: reproduced to within about 200 cm-1 of experimentally derived values, which is usually under 10 percent error for 4dn, 5dn and 4fn configurations but up to 30 percent for 3dn; the abstract-level summary is overestimation by 5-30 percent for 3d ions, within plus or minus 10 percent for 4d and 5d ions, and overestimation by 2-10 percent for trivalent 4f ions. Slater-Condon parameters are typically overestimated by 20-50 percent (with some 3d outliers underestimated by 1-20 percent) because of the missing dynamic correlation, so the authors explicitly do not recommend minimal active space CASSCF-SO where accurate term excitation energies are needed, and recommend CASPT2 or NEVPT2 instead for quantitative work. The Slater-Condon error is systematic for divalent 4d and trivalent 4f ions, so simple scaling may be viable there when resources are limited, but this does not hold for 3d ions. The spin-orbit coupling constant varies quadratically with atomic number Z at fixed dn configuration, and also for the trivalent lanthanides even though the configuration changes with Z; SOC detail: yes, spin-orbit coupling introduced by state interaction after variational spin-free orbital optimization

compound_name: QUESTDB benchmark database - 542 vertical excitation energies with automated APC active-space selection
point_group: reduced to the highest available symmetry implementable for each molecule
geometry_source: QUESTDB benchmark geometries
method: state-averaged CASSCF with MC-PDFT (tPBE) and NEVPT2, using automated entropy-ranked active-space selection
active_space_orbital_description: Automated 'max(n,m)' spaces capped by a maximum CSF count: max(4,4) (N_max_CSF = 20), max(5,5), max(12,12) and others. Orbitals are ranked by occupancy and entropy pairs (n_j, S_j) and pruned until the CSF count falls under the cap.
active_space_protocol: Approximate pair-coefficient (APC) automated selection with a 'max(n,m)' cap set by a maximum CSF count: orbitals carry an occupancy and an approximated entropy (n_j, S_j) and are admitted in entropy order until the CSF count would exceed N_max_CSF. A worked example takes a max(4,4) target (cap 20 CSFs) and returns a (5,4) space with exactly 20 CSFs. Critically, the authors then FILTER: 20-30% of the automatically generated active spaces were poor and were eliminated by applying a threshold to the SA-CASSCF absolute error, leaving 373 of the 542 excitations for the method comparison.
electronic_structure_description: Largest benchmarking of MC-PDFT and HMC-PDFT to date, over the QUESTDB set of 542 vertical excitations. After discarding the 20-30% of automatically chosen active spaces that were poor, HMC-PDFT performs about as well as NEVPT2 and CC2 on the remaining 373 excitations. The optimal fraction of SA-CASSCF energy to mix into HMC-PDFT with the tPBE on-top functional was found to be 25%, i.e. the value already used in tPBE0. NEVPT2 performance is significantly affected by active-space quality, and at normal grid size tPBE is on average about 114x cheaper than NEVPT2 for large max(12,12) spaces.

method: CASSCF references followed by CASPT2 and CASPT3, both with and without the IPEA shift (default 0.25 Eh) and with a 0.3 a.u. level shift, plus partially contracted and strongly contracted NEVPT2; the Fock operator in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian is systematically built from the state-specific density. Benchmarked against selected-CI (CIPSI) and the high-order coupled cluster hierarchy EOM-CC3, EOM-CCSDT, EOM-CC4 and EOM-CCSDTQ, with the %T1 diagnostic from CC3/AVTZ used to classify a state as singly or doubly excited
software: molpro for the multiconfigurational calculations (dalton also used)

active_space_protocol: active spaces are chosen individually for each system, each symmetry representation and each transition, following the protocol of the authors' earlier work; the SI carries the complete listing. The paper stresses that careful selection is what makes doubly excited states reachable at manageable cost, and that 0.1-0.2 eV accuracy is achievable with appropriate spaces. Whether the 3s Rydberg orbital is included in the space materially changes the answer: leave it out and a single genuine double excitation appears, put it in and the doubly excited configuration mixes with the Rydberg one.
electronic_structure_description: For one of the difficult cases the two computed states at 7.979(40) and 8.170(41) eV from CIPSI agree well with the reference 7.979 and 8.185 eV. Both states carry important singly and doubly excited configurations, combined in phase for the lower state and out of phase for the upper one; the mixing is weak at CASSCF and becomes pronounced only after the perturbative correction. Enlarging the basis from 6-31+G* to aug-cc-pVDZ or aug-cc-pVTZ stabilizes the (n -> 3s) Rydberg configuration relative to the (n,n -> pi*,pi*) one and suppresses the strong mixing - 6-31+G* is simply too compact to model it. Downgrading to CC4 or CCSDT also unmixes the two configurations, giving one genuine double and one Rydberg single; oddly the mixing returns at CC3, but for the wrong reason.

compound_name: Thiel's benchmark set of 28 closed-shell organic molecules: 223 vertical excitation energies evaluated with fourth-order NEVPT
formula: the 28 closed-shell organic molecules of the Thiel benchmark set
geometry_source: the geometries of the original Thiel benchmark study
method: approximate fourth-order N-electron valence perturbation theory, NEVPT4(SD): the fully internally contracted fourth-order NEVPT with the excitation space restricted to the first-order interacting space of internally contracted singles and doubles from the CASSCF reference, with the fourth-order renormalization terms dropped to keep size consistency in the absence of quadruples; compared against lower-order NEVPT variants, published CASPT2 results, and CC3 reference data
active_space_orbital_description: the active spaces of the earlier NEVPT study of Schapiro et al. on this benchmark set, chosen per molecule and not restated here
active_space_protocol: the protocol follows Schapiro et al., with state-averaged CASSCF used whenever several roots of the same symmetry are needed; although ORCA can state-average across different spatial and spin symmetries, the calculations were deliberately run separately per symmetry to allow direct comparison with the original work. Two protocols for the vertical energies: for excitations within the ground-state irreducible representation the ground-state energy comes from the state-averaged calculation, and a different route is used otherwise.
electronic_structure_description: Across 223 vertical excitation energies spanning pi -> pi*, n -> pi* and sigma -> pi* transitions in 28 molecules, NEVPT4(SD) systematically outperforms both the lower-order NEVPT variants and previously reported CASPT2 results, for singlets and triplets alike. The residual error is structured rather than random: n -> pi* transitions are overestimated by about 0.1 eV while pi -> pi* transitions are underestimated by about 0.04 eV. That shift persists at every NEVPT order but shrinks as the order increases.

formula: the organic molecules of the Schreiber et al. benchmark set
geometry_source: the geometries of the Schreiber et al. benchmark set
method: adiabatic connection (AC) correlation energy methods AC0 and AC0D built on extended random phase approximation (ERPA) with complete active space reference wave functions, plus a new perturbation-corrected ERPA transition density matrix for the oscillator strengths; benchmarked against CASPT2, LR-CC2, LR-CCSD, CCSD and FCI values
basis_set: the basis sets of the Schreiber et al. benchmark protocol (TZVP)

active_space_protocol: state-averaged CASSCF reference states from the ground state up to the target state I are required for an AC0D excitation energy; because AC0 and AC0D depend only on reduced density matrices up to second order, they scale far better in the number of active orbitals than CASPT2 and NEVPT2, whose cost confines them in practice to roughly 20 active electrons
electronic_structure_description: Oscillator strengths computed from the perturbation-corrected ERPA transition density matrices, together with AC0 and AC0D excitation energies, match CASPT2 accuracy at lower cost, and the corrected transition dipole moments come essentially free because every intermediate is already available from the AC0 energy calculation. For triplet excitations on the Schreiber set, the deexcitation correction in AC0D genuinely improves on AC0, especially for the lowest excited states, where the accuracy becomes comparable to LR-CC2 and LR-CCSD - with the difference that AC0 and AC0D remain multireference methods. The perturbation-corrected transition density matrices also beat the uncorrected ERPA ones against CCSD and FCI in matching basis sets.

electronic_structure_description: The TBEs/aug-cc-pVTZ assembled here benchmark a long list of lower-order wave function methods: CIS(D), ADC(2), CC2, STEOM-CCSD, CCSD, CCSDR(3), CCSDT-3, ADC(3), CC3, NEVPT2 and their spin-scaled variants. The accuracy of CASPT2 and NEVPT2 turns out to be the hardest to predict of any method in the set, because it depends on both the system and the chosen active space; the pattern that does emerge is that they are more accurate for transitions with a very small percentage of single-excitation character (error usually below 0.1 eV) than for the single-excitation-dominated ones, where the error approaches 0.1-0.2 eV. The whole data set is published through a website.
reference_short: Veril, Scemama, Caffarel, Loos, Jacquemin et al., QUESTDB: a database of highly accurate excitation energies for the electronic structure community

active_space_orbital_description: Six pi electrons distributed among twelve pi orbitals. Starting from the six-valence-pi-orbital CAS (three bonding pi plus three antibonding pi* orbitals), the authors doubled the active orbital count in every symmetry. The paper does not print a complete symmetry-by-symmetry list of the six added pi orbitals. Sigma electrons remain outside the CAS and their dynamic sigma-pi polarization is introduced by MRMP.
active_space_protocol: (6,6): six pi electrons in the six valence pi/pi* orbitals; (6,12): active orbital count doubled in every symmetry and the same state calculations repeated. This row records the converged extended (6,12) results.

electronic_structure_description: The enlarged pi space primarily improves the ionic plus states by moving part of the important sigma-pi polarization/nondynamical response into the reference. Covalent-state CASSCF energies change little, while ionic-state CASSCF excitations decrease by about 0.3-0.5 eV. The resulting MRMP spectrum reaches <=0.23 eV error for the tabulated singlets and <=0.29 eV for triplets. Detailed CASSCF configuration coefficients are printed only for the smaller CAS(6,6), not for this extended reference.
Other: TOTAL ENERGY: ground-state MRMP energy with twelve active pi orbitals = -231.62903 Eh; the authors note that the smaller-space MRMP energy is paradoxically 0.00170 Eh lower because second-order perturbation theory can overestimate correlation when its zeroth-order Hamiltonian is incomplete. active_space_orbital_description: The same minimal seven-electron seven-orbital and eleven-electron nine-orbital spaces as the quartet, enlarged along a different sequence: eleven orbitals adding virtuals with iron dxz and dxy character, twelve adding one with dyz character, and finally fourteen including the fourth iron dz2 double-shell orbital together with an additional empty ligand orbital.
active_space_protocol: The same construction and enlargement strategy as for the quartet but with a different order of orbital admission, reflecting which double-shell orbitals could be stabilised in this state. The largest space contains the four iron dxz, dxy, dyz and dz2 double-shell orbitals. The contributions of the iron double-shell orbitals to the natural orbitals are noted to be significantly larger for this state than for the quartet.
electronic_structure_description: For the doublet state the spin density shows larger deviations with respect to the size of the active space than the quartet does, converging gradually toward the largest reference as the space is enlarged. The minimal seven-electron seven-orbital and eleven-electron nine-orbital spaces, without double-shell orbitals, are qualitatively similar to the reference and suffice for a qualitative estimate, but quantitatively correct spin densities require the iron double-shell orbitals to be included. Spaces containing thirteen active electrons give very similar spin densities. The same bonding picture applies as for the quartet, with one iron d orbital non-interacting and three interacting covalently with the nitrosyl orbitals.
Other: The space is built up from a qualitative molecular orbital picture: four metal 3d orbitals plus both nitrosyl pi-star orbitals, extended by a fifth metal d orbital, giving a minimal seven electrons in seven orbitals; adding both nitrosyl pi orbitals gives eleven electrons in nine orbitals. It is then systematically enlarged toward a double shell, one metal d orbital at a time, through eleven, twelve, thirteen and fifteen orbitals for the quartet and eleven, twelve and fourteen for the doublet. The obstacles encountered are reported rather than glossed: identifying the double-shell orbitals is described as not trivial because they mix considerably with antibonding ligand orbitals, so additional ligand orbitals had to be admitted to keep the space stable; in one case a double-shell orbital rotated into an empty ligand orbital and a further virtual had to be added to recover it; the fifth metal double-shell orbital could not be included at all because its destabilization by the point-charge environment would require many more ligand orbitals; and an alternative route adding a ligand sigma and sigma-star pair proved incompatible with including the remaining double-shell orbitals. The result is that convergence depends on which state is asked about. For the quartet the spin density depends only weakly on the space, and the minimal seven-orbital and nine-orbital calculations without any double-shell effect already agree qualitatively with the largest reference. For the doublet the deviations are larger, the spin density converging gradually toward the reference as the space grows, and the authors state the distinction precisely: the minimal spaces suffice for a qualitative estimate while quantitatively correct spin densities require the metal double-shell orbitals. Consistently, the double-shell contributions to the natural orbitals are noted to be significantly larger for the doublet than for the quartet. So the same molecule, same property, different spin state, and the answer to whether a double shell is needed flips. The bonding picture the space reveals is stable across all of them: one metal d orbital does not interact with the ligand at all, while three others interact strongly and covalently with the nitrosyl orbitals to give two bonding, two antibonding and one nonbonding combination. One structural caveat: the ligand field is modelled by point charges rather than real ligands, and the authors note that the modelled field is not strong enough, so the environment that destabilises the fifth double-shell orbital is itself an approximation.

point_group: C2v used for the CASSCF calculations
geometry_source: Optimized with the B3PW91 functional in the BS-I basis, with vibrational frequencies confirming minima and transition states; the CASSCF calculations were single points in BS-II on those geometries
method: CASSCF used as a diagnostic of multireference character on species from a reaction path otherwise computed by density functional theory; geometries and frequencies from the hybrid functional, energies re-evaluated in the larger basis
software: MOLCAS 6.0 for the CASSCF calculations; Gaussian 03 for the density functional work and NBO 3.1 for population analysis
basis_set: BS-II: cc-pVDZ on carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and hydrogen with a Stuttgart-Dresden-Bonn effective core potential and a (311111/22111/411) valence basis on ruthenium
active_space_orbital_description: Fourteen orbitals itemized by symmetry block as five a1, three b1, three a2 and three b2, chosen by three stated rules: all ruthenium 4d orbitals, the ruthenium 5d-like orbitals that correlate with them for the double-shell effect, and the four Gouterman porphyrin pi orbitals (two occupied in a1 and b2, two unoccupied in a2 and b1).
active_space_protocol: The same fourteen orbitals are used for every species in the series, with only the electron count changed to follow the charge, so that comparisons between oxidation states cannot be an artifact of a different orbital choice.
electronic_structure_description: Much less stable than the singlet, by 48.4 kcal/mol. Its geometry was optimized separately with the unrestricted functional. The leading configuration carries 89.40% of the weight, the largest of the five species, and assigns ruthenium +II.
Other: The active space here is specified by three stated rules rather than by a number, and the rules are what make the five species comparable. All ruthenium 4d orbitals and their electrons must be in the space; the ruthenium 5d-like orbitals that correlate with them must also be in, to capture the double-shell effect; and the four porphyrin pi orbitals of the classic Gouterman set -- two occupied, in the totally symmetric and one of the antisymmetric blocks, and two unoccupied -- must be in. That gives fourteen orbitals, itemized by symmetry block as five, three, three and three, and the SAME fourteen orbitals are used for the neutral singlet, the neutral triplet, the cation and the anion, with only the electron count changing to follow the charge: fourteen, fourteen, thirteen and fifteen. Holding the orbital set fixed while the electron count tracks the charge is exactly the design needed to compare oxidation states, since any difference between species then cannot be blamed on a different choice of orbitals. Only for the oxo anion is the set enlarged, by one further orbital added specifically to represent the ruthenium-oxygen antibonding interaction -- an enlargement made because a specific bond is being broken, not to recover more correlation. The space is used as a DIAGNOSTIC rather than as a source of energetics. The reported result is that the leading configuration carries more than 85% of the weight in every one of the five species (85.66, 89.40, 88.80, 88.02 and 85.65 percent), from which the authors conclude static correlation is small and a single-determinant method is adequate; they further check that the natural orbitals from the unrestricted density functional calculation are essentially the same as the multiconfigurational ones. Two independent checks pointing the same way is a stronger licence for the cheaper method than either alone. The second finding is chemical and cuts against the experimental proposal that motivated the calculation: the leading configuration assigns ruthenium the +II oxidation state in ALL five species, including the cation and both anions, so the experimentally proposed +I-to-+III change is not what the wave function shows -- the added or removed electron sits on the porphyrin ring, not on the metal. The scope limit is that these are CASSCF wave functions with no perturbative correction, so the weights speak to static correlation only, and a fourteen-orbital space concentrated on the metal d shell and the Gouterman four cannot report multireference character arising anywhere outside it. The calculations were run in the smaller correlation-consistent basis under C2v symmetry even for the species whose optimized geometry is C4v.

active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in eight active orbitals: the six ring pi orbitals, the nitrogen lone pair (pN), and the sigma orbital located at the divalent carbon atom C1.
active_space_protocol: CASSCF was run for an explicitly diagnostic purpose — "to check the viability of such a single-determinant approach and to describe the nature of the singlet and triplet H2NC6H4+" — after the bulk of the study had been done at B3LYP. The test is the weight of the ground-state reference determinant in the CASSCF wave function, read from the coefficient of the lowest eigenvector and from the fractional populations of the eight active orbitals. The same test had been applied to the parent phenyl cation, where the reference determinant contributes more than 90% (eigenvector coefficients 0.94 for the singlet and 0.95 for the triplet), justifying B3LYP there.
electronic_structure_description: Excited singlet lying at least 10 kcal/mol above the triplet in the gas phase. Its CASSCF wave function "is poorly described by any single configuration" and cannot be properly represented by a single determinant, so the B3LYP description of this state is not reliable — in contrast to the parent phenyl cation, whose singlet has a reference determinant weight above 90% (eigenvector coefficient 0.94). Geometrically the singlet differs from the planar triplet: the nitrogen is slightly pyramidalized and the divalent carbon C1 is slightly bent out of plane and puckered.
Other: The (8,8) space — six ring pi orbitals, the nitrogen lone pair, and the sigma orbital on the divalent carbon — is used to answer a single question: can a single-determinant method be trusted for this ion? The answer differs by spin state, and that difference is the paper's finding. For the 3B2 triplet the CASSCF wave function is dominated by one configuration, with the leading coefficient above 0.93 and fractional populations of the eight active orbitals close to 0, 1 and 2 — so B3LYP is adequate there, and indeed the CASSCF and UB3LYP geometries and charges "are in excellent agreement only for the 3B2 state". For the 1A' singlet the wave function "is poorly described by any single configuration" and "cannot be properly described by a single-determinant" treatment, so the B3LYP singlet results are not reliable. This is a clean case of an active space being used to bound the validity of a cheaper method rather than to produce numbers. The orbital populations also carry chemical content that a single-determinant picture would hide: in the triplet, the sigma and one pi orbital are each singly occupied, with the sigma electron highly localized on C1 but the pi electron delocalized over the ring and onto nitrogen. Combined with UB3LYP spin densities showing nitrogen carrying the second highest spin density (0.35), this makes the triplet "65% diradical, 35% carbene character at divalent C1" — which explains why it does not react with neutral sigma nucleophiles (there is no cation at C1, the largest positive charge being +0.37 on C4) but adds readily to pi nucleophiles as an electrophilic radical. For the parent phenyl cation the same diagnostic gave >90% single-reference character for BOTH states, so amino substitution is what breaks the single-determinant description of the singlet.

The starting reference configuration is (9a1)2(6b2)2(1b1)2(2b1)2(1a2)1, and the same active space is used as for the lower component. In the optimized geometry only the carbon-carbon bond perpendicular to the binary symmetry axis shows double-bond character, in contrast to the diene-like structure of the lower component. Its total energy is -193.146453 hartree, and in combination with the magnesium cation -392.510536 hartree, giving a binding energy of 74.3 kcal/mol against 74.0 for the lower component. The geometry agrees with previous theoretical work on the same footing as the lower component.

That is precisely the situation a single-determinant method cannot handle, and it is why this fragment alone is treated multiconfigurationally while everything else in the study, including the magnesium complexes that are its subject, is handled by single-reference perturbation and composite methods. The space is specified by symmetry block rather than by total: five valence electrons distributed over four orbitals of b1 symmetry and two of a2 symmetry. Crucially the same space is used for both Jahn-Teller components, each started from its own open-shell reference configuration, which is what makes the small energy difference between them meaningful -- the two states differ by which orbital carries the single electron, and comparing them across differently constructed spaces would confound the splitting with the reference. The validation is a proper enlargement test with a stated criterion. The space was extended by one further virtual orbital of each symmetry, and the resulting optimized geometry came out close to the original; the authors connect the two observations by noting that the added orbitals carry insignificant occupation numbers, less than 0.003. Reporting the occupation numbers rather than just the geometric agreement is what turns this from an assertion into evidence, since an orbital with occupation below 0.003 cannot be contributing to the wave function regardless of what the geometry does. active_space_protocol: Full valence active space - six electrons in six orbitals - used identically for the state-specific multiconfigurational calculations, for the state-averaged orbitals feeding the configuration-interaction spin-orbit step, and for the coupling calculation inside the functional-based dynamics. Because the program cannot compute spin-orbit coupling from density functional theory, that coupling is obtained from a configuration-interaction calculation in the same space using the high-spin alpha functional orbitals, so the active space is not eliminated even in the nominally functional treatment. No spatial symmetry restrictions are imposed during the simulations.

geometry_source: Optimized directly at the CASSCF level under a Cs symmetry constraint
method: CASSCF potential energy surface scans and geometry optimizations, with second-order multireference Moller-Plesset perturbation corrections computed at several conformations including all valence and virtual orbitals; the conical intersection was optimized in a reduced space and verified in the larger one
software: GAMESS for most calculations; Gaussian 03 for the conical intersection optimization
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning double-zeta with polarization functions added on the skeletal carbons (exponent 0.75) and on nitrogen (exponent 0.80), a double-zeta plus polarization quality set; the polarization functions on the skeletal carbons are stated to be necessary to obtain a reasonable intersection
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in the highest five occupied and lowest five unoccupied pi orbitals. These were selected from all seven occupied and lowest seven unoccupied pi orbitals by a configuration interaction calculation including up to triple excitations, discarding the two lowest occupied orbitals whose occupations exceeded 1.98 and the two highest unoccupied whose occupations fell below 0.02, a criterion verified for all sampled conformations.
active_space_protocol: Reduced in two stages from the fourteen-electron fourteen-orbital full pi space, declared desirable but unrealistic for surface scanning. The ten-orbital space serves the scans and the minima; an eight-orbital space, justified by the same preliminary calculation, was used for the conical intersection search and then checked by a ten-orbital calculation at the located geometry confirming the state gap remained small enough. All work is confined to Cs symmetry, so a planar structure has C2v symmetry and nonplanar distortion is allowed only within the mirror plane.
nroots_per_mult: the ground and first excited singlet states
electronic_structure_description: The relaxed geometry on the first excited singlet surface, optimized in the same ten-orbital space under the Cs constraint. The excited molecule reaches this region after vertical excitation and then travels onward to the intersection with the ground state.
Other: The space here is arrived at by a two-stage reduction from a stated ideal, with each stage justified numerically rather than by assertion, and the criterion is occupation numbers taken from an independent calculation. The desirable space is named first: fourteen electrons in fourteen orbitals, since the molecule has fourteen pi electrons, ten from the bicyclic skeleton and four from the nitrile group. That is declared unrealistic for scanning potential energy surfaces, so a configuration interaction calculation including up to triple excitations was run over all seven occupied and the lowest seven unoccupied pi orbitals, and the resulting occupation numbers used to prune. The lowest two occupied orbitals came out above 1.98 and the highest two unoccupied below 0.02, so those four were dropped, leaving ten electrons in ten orbitals. The crucial detail is that the occupation criterion was checked for all sampled conformations, not just at equilibrium -- a space pruned on occupation numbers at one geometry can easily fail elsewhere on a surface that runs to a conical intersection, and the authors closed that gap explicitly. A second reduction follows for the intersection search alone, down to eight electrons in eight orbitals on the basis of the same preliminary calculation showing that four occupied and four unoccupied pi orbitals suffice where the two states are nearly degenerate. This one is validated after the fact rather than before: the intersection was optimized in the eight-orbital space, then a ten-orbital calculation was performed at that geometry and the gap between the two states confirmed small enough to still be an intersection. Optimizing in a small space and verifying in a larger one at the located point is a cheap and honest way to use a reduced space for a geometry search, and the authors draw the right conclusion, that the larger space would give a similar structure rather than that it would give the same one. The whole scheme rests on a symmetry constraint that is itself a modelling choice: calculations are confined to Cs, so a planar structure has the full two-fold symmetry while nonplanar distortions are permitted only within the mirror plane. Since the central question is whether the intersection is nonplanar in the seven-membered ring, constraining the allowed distortions is a substantive restriction, and the paper devotes an appendix to defending it. A second appendix defends the basis: polarization functions on the skeletal carbons are stated to be necessary to obtain a reasonable intersection at all for this family of molecules, so the intersection geometry is sensitive to the one-electron basis as well as to the space. Dynamical correlation enters only as single-point corrections at several conformations, with all valence and virtual orbitals included in the perturbation, so the surfaces that were scanned and the geometries that were optimized carry no correlation beyond the ten-orbital space.

method: CASSCF conical intersection and intersystem crossing point optimization; TD-B3LYP for excited-state minima and vertical excitations
active_space_orbital_description: CASSCF(8,7) for the S1(1npi*)/T1(3pipi*) intersystem crossing: seven active orbitals comprising one nO, three pi, two pi* and one RYDBERG orbital — a different selection from the conical-intersection space, dropping the sigma/sigma* pair and adding a diffuse orbital.

electronic_structure_description: The Sn/T1(3pipi*) intersystem crossing point lies 85.5 kcal/mol above S0 at CASSCF(8,7)/6-31G(d) — well below the Sn/Spi conical intersection at 130 kcal/mol. The decay picture that follows is that the initially populated Spi state relaxes to the lower-lying Sn state and then crosses to T1(3pipi*) through this point.
Other: Two DIFFERENT (8,7) spaces are used for the two crossing points, each built around the orbitals the specific crossing needs, and the substitution is stated explicitly. For the S1(1npi*)/S2(1pipi*) CONICAL INTERSECTION the seven orbitals are one nO, one sigma(C-N), two pi, two pi* and one sigma*(C-N) — the sigma/sigma* pair being included because the intersection involves C-N stretching. For the S1(1npi*)/T1(3pipi*) INTERSYSTEM CROSSING the seven orbitals are instead one nO, three pi, two pi* and one RYDBERG orbital, dropping the sigma/sigma* pair entirely and adding a diffuse function. So the two crossing energies quoted on the same kcal/mol scale relative to S0 — 130 for the conical intersection and 85.5 for the intersystem crossing — come from different orbital selections and are not strictly one surface. The paper is candid about the limit on validating this: "due to the limited computational resources, we are unable to check the Sn/Spi conical intersection point at any higher theoretical level", so no convergence test against a larger space or a correlated method was performed for the intersection that carries the mechanistic argument. Everything else in the study rests on TD-B3LYP rather than CASSCF — the excited-state minima, the vertical excitation energies and the resonance Raman intensity analysis — with CASSCF used only where a single-reference method cannot go, namely at the two crossing points. Note the resulting scale mismatch: the Sn and Spi minima are placed 93 and 107 kcal/mol above S0 by TD-B3LYP while the crossings between them are placed at 130 and 85.5 kcal/mol by CASSCF, so the relative ordering of minima and funnels mixes two levels of theory.

DMU shows lambda-max = 266 nm in water, red-shifted 7 nm from uracil's 259 nm because of hyperconjugation between the methyl group and the pi(H) orbital; 5BrDMU absorbs at 280 nm in acetonitrile, a further 16 nm red shift attributed to the antibonding interaction between the bromine p(z) orbital and the DMU pi orbital raising the donor orbital energy. Computed singlet transitions at 232 nm (f = 0.1495) and 201 nm (f = 0.1273) correlate with the observed A-band at 264 nm (f = 0.2369) and B-band at 206 nm (f = 0.3695). Both molecules have 48 normal modes, and this work provides the first vibrational assignments for either. The Sn and Spi excited-state minima, computed at TD-B3LYP/6-31G(d), lie 93 and 107 kcal/mol above S0 and 14.9 and 10.3 kcal/mol below their respective Franck-Condon points; Sn is a relatively pure 1npi* state while Spi is noticeably mixed with Sn.

method: CASSCF/CASPT2 vertical excitation energies at DFT geometries, with level shifting to remove intruder states; B3LYP and time-dependent B3LYP used alongside
software: MOLCAS 4 for all CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 98 for the DFT work; ACES II for a CCSD(T) optimization

active_space_protocol: Three a' orbitals were added to the eight a''-type pi and pi* orbitals specifically because the characteristic triplet nitrene absorption involves excitation from the sp lone pair into the singly occupied in-plane 2p orbital of nitrogen. The total space size is held at (12,11), matching the singlet, so the symmetry composition changes while the size does not. Level shifting was applied in the CASPT2 step as for the singlet, with 0.25 au used for the tabulated energies.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1 3A'', with 83 percent of the ground configuration. Table 4 gives vertical excitation energies from CASSCF(12,11)/CASPT2 at the B3LYP/6-31G* geometry: 1 3A' at 0.45 and 1.60 eV, weight 0.76, 775 nm, f 1.3e-4, 80 percent 26a' to 5a''; 2 3A'' at 3.21 and 2.93 eV, weight 0.74, 424 nm, f 1.4e-2, 34 percent 4a'' to 5a'' with 21 percent 4a'' to 6a''; 3 3A'' at 3.76 and 3.04 eV, weight 0.74, 407 nm, f 5.6e-3, 72 percent 23a' to 27a'; 4 3A'' at 3.81 and 3.21 eV, weight 0.74, 386 nm, f 4.6e-3, 44 percent 3a'' to 5a''; 5 3A'' at 4.34 and 3.75 eV, weight 0.74, 330 nm, f 2.6e-2, 36 percent 3a'' to 7a''; 6 3A'' at 4.61 and 4.32 eV, weight 0.74, 287 nm, f 6.4e-3, 37 percent 3a'' to 6a''; 7 3A'' at 4.98 and 4.42 eV, weight 0.74, 280 nm, f 2.2e-2; 2 3A' at 3.38 and 4.48 eV, weight 0.76, 277 nm, f 1.4e-4, 35 percent 27a' to 6a''; and 3 3A' at 4.03 and 5.15 eV, weight 0.76, 241 nm, f 1.2e-5. The triplet is predicted to have several intense absorption bands in the visible and near ultraviolet, a spectrum showing no relation to the experimental one, which the authors take as confirming the absence of the triplet nitrene among the products of photolysis.
Other: The two spin states are treated in spaces of identical size, (12,11), but of deliberately different symmetry composition, and the paper explains why. For the singlet the space contains nine a'' and two a' orbitals -- essentially the pi system. For the triplet the balance shifts to eight a'' and three a', and the reason is stated explicitly: the triplet's characteristic absorption involves excitation of an electron from the sp lone pair orbital into the singly occupied in-plane 2p orbital of nitrogen, a transition analogous to those seen from the triplet ground states of NH at 336 nm, methylnitrene at 315 nm, perfluoromethylnitrene at 354 nm and 1-norbornylnitrene at 298 nm. To describe it, three a' orbitals were added -- the singly occupied in-plane p orbital of nitrogen and two combinations of the in-plane oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs -- to the eight a''-type pi and pi* orbitals. So one orbital was traded out of the pi block to admit the in-plane orbital the transition actually uses. This is a clean example of the space being chosen by which transitions must be representable rather than by a uniform recipe, and of holding the total size fixed so that the two states' reference weights remain comparable: they sit at 0.74 to 0.77 across both tables. The consequence for the paper's conclusion is direct. The computed triplet spectrum shows several intense bands in the visible and near ultraviolet that bear no relation to the experimental spectrum, and that mismatch is what the authors take as confirming the absence of the triplet nitrene among the photolysis products. A negative identification of this kind is only as good as the space's ability to produce those bands in the first place, which is precisely why the in-plane orbitals had to be admitted. A second and independent caveat concerns intruder states rather than orbital selection. To obtain a satisfactory description of all excited states at the CASPT2 level it was necessary to resort to level shifting, and the authors state that they carefully assured no artifacts were introduced, reporting in supplementary tables the results of calculations with level shifts ranging from 0 to 0.3 au; the tabulated energies use 0.25 au. That is the right way to use a level shift -- scanned and reported rather than fixed by default -- but it means the excitation energies carry a chosen parameter, and a few entries show how much CASSCF and CASPT2 can disagree in a single reference: for the triplet the 2 3A' state moves from 3.38 eV at CASSCF up to 4.48 eV at CASPT2, and the 3 3A' state from 4.03 to 5.15 eV, both shifting upward while every other state shifts downward. Finally, note that the multiconfigurational treatment was applied only at geometries obtained elsewhere, at the B3LYP/6-31G* level, and that the electronic spectra of the substituted acetyl derivative were predicted with time-dependent DFT rather than with this space at all.
